incident-bot: Pager: kvcache.oom.hosted triggered on node pool hosted-runtime-2 at 4232101234. Reason: sustained KV cache growth from long prompt streams -> OOM. Priority: P1. Paging oncall for hosted-runtime.

alex (runtime oncall): I’m on it. seeing repeated OOMs on gpu-node-17, process=runtime-serving, oom_kvcache. Logs show large prefix growth from a few sessions.

mari (ml): likely continuous-prefetch + large context combos. We pushed a quantized model yesterday; could change memory layout but this looks like prefix amplification, not model size.

alex (runtime oncall): stack trace snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T10:01:02Z] OOM: kvmap alloc failed: requested 1536MB, free 0MB
[2026-03-15T10:01:02Z] evict_loop: unable to evict, pinned keys 48
[2026-03-15T10:01:02Z] process runtime-serving pid=7821 crashed (killed by OOM)
```

jordan (sre): Health signals: hosted runtime error-rate up 7x, p50 latency +400ms, p95 skyrockets. Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream (hosted), a few customers reporting 5xx.

ingrid (support): I’m seeing support tickets for two customers complaining of repeated "server error" and failed responses. One is an enterprise account on dedicated plans? (checking) — actually both are hosted customers on large-model plan.

alex (runtime oncall): mitigation plan: 1) disable continuous prefetch for hosted tier globally 2) reduce runtime batch window tokens to 512 3) roll a hotpatch that forces KV cache eviction to be more aggressive (lower eviction threshold). Doing them in that order to avoid restart last.

mari (ml): Agree, disabling prefetch should stop prefix growth right away. We might still need a rolling restart of the runtime pods to free leaked KV memory.

alex (runtime oncall): Executing config toggle now. Command: ```bash
# disable prefetch for hosted by flipping feature flag
redwood-config set hosted.kvcache.prefetch.enabled false --reason "pager 4232101234"
```

deploy-bot: config update queued -> hosted.kvcache.prefetch.enabled=false. Rolling apply to runtime-config service.

alex (runtime oncall): Confirmed flag hit runtimes, observing drop in prefetch requests in metrics. Prefetch RPS down 98% on hosted pool.

jordan (sre): Next: reduce batch window. Patch command: ```bash
kubectl -n runtime patch deployment runtime-serving -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","env":[{"name":"BATCH_MAX_TOKENS","value":"512"}]}]}}}}'
I’ll kick the rolling restart after patch so pods pickup new env.

alex (runtime oncall): Doing a staggered 2-at-a-time restart to avoid cold-start surge.

ingrid (support): Customer impact update: ~5 hosted customers affected intermittently, two support tickets escalated to SLM. No confirmed data loss, requests either 5xx or high latency and timeouts.

sam (product): Heads-up to account teams: customers A and B might hit retries. If we have an ETA for fix, tell them 1-2 hours for full stabilization after restarts.

alex (runtime oncall): Hotpatch ready for eviction tweaks. Plan: lower kv_eviction_threshold from 0.75 -> 0.5 to force earlier evictions, and reduce max_cached_segments per session to 4. Applying now with minimal restarts.

deploy-bot: hotpatch applied to runtime-serving config: kv_eviction_threshold=0.5, max_cached_segments=4. No full cluster restart required.

alex (runtime oncall): Metrics: memory usage on gpu-node-17 dropped ~35% within 6 minutes. OOMs stopped on that node. Error-rate for /v1/chat/stream down to 1.3x baseline, still slightly elevated.

mari (ml): Good. We should also add a short-term guard: drop requests with prefix length > 120k tokens for hosted tier (respond with 413 / short-circuit) — avoids repeated heavy tails.

jordan (sre): Implemented guard at ingress: `if prefix_tokens > 120000 then return 413`. This is a soft-fail for hosted; logged for customers. Patch rolled.

alex (runtime oncall): Confirm ingress guard active. We’re still seeing a few noisy sessions that caused the initial spike; those sessions are being throttled/closed by the guard.

ingrid (support): Sent proactive messages to affected customers with mitigation steps; letting them know guard is in place and we’re monitoring.
